method: blind-execute, held in full. (1) Only id/prompt/files were extracted, with jq, into the suite-prefixed file rebase-serp-prompts.json — no sibling field (expectations, expected_output) was ever on screen during execution. (2) Evals were executed in order 1..5; for each I read only that eval's prompt and its fixture, loaded SKILL.md plus all six references, produced the complete client deliverable and SAVED it. (3) research/serp-analysis/evals/evals.json was opened for the FIRST time only after all five deliverables were saved; no eval's expectations were read ahead of its own execution, and none was read before its deliverable existed. (4) No deliverable was edited after its expectations were read — three defects spotted on re-read are recorded in self_caught and left in the artefacts. (5) The prior serp baseline record inside docs/loop/eval-baselines/2026-08-10-e2345.json was NOT opened until grading was complete; only the suite-name list and the serp entry's key names were read at launch, via jq, to establish that a baseline existed. (6) build/seo-content-writer/references/anti-slop-ruleset.md §6 was read only at grading time, after the Greek deliverable was written and saved, so the seven ruled families did not steer the Greek output. DISCOUNT, stated because the 2026-08-10 baseline demands it: the launching task message named the Greek checker traps (LC_ALL case-folding, synizesis monosyllables, enclitic double accents, wc -w) and told me §6 has seven families. That is briefing about the GRADING instrument, not about what the evals test or what the skill should get right, and no serp-specific trap was named — but this run is blind to expectation wording, not cold.
